Now [[Endor (Dark){{!}}Endor]] gives us [[Ominous Rumors]], another Effect that can have an entire deck strategy built around it. As with the other Force drain bonus cards, this one requires a balanced deck; control of both battleground systems and [[Endor (Dark){{!}}Endor]] sites. The payoff is increased Force drains in space, a feature where the Dark side has struggled in the past. Meeting the basic requirements of [[Ominous Rumors]] will give the Dark side a Force drain of 4 at the [[Endor (Dark){{!}}Endor]] system! As with EBO, the Imperials must retain control of [[Endor (Dark){{!}}Endor]] sites to keep [[Ominous Rumors]] in play. This Effect may have limited value in [[Endor (Dark){{!}}Endor]] booster draft play, since it must be deployed before the Light side controls any [[Endor (Dark){{!}}Endor]] sites, and there are only 3 systems available in the expansion. If a player was fortunate enought to get [[Ominous Rumors]] up and running, however, they would drain their opponent out very quickly. It is also one of the two staple cards required to flip your [[Endor Operations / Imperial Outpost{{!}}Endor Operations]] objective. Combos: - will give a Light side [[Hidden Base / Systems Will Slip Through Your Fingers{{!}}Hidden Base]] deck some serious trouble. Spread out, probe and drain with TIEs without fear of battle damage. - At the [[Endor: Bunker (Dark){{!}}Endor: Bunker]] or any [[Endor (Dark){{!}}Endor]] battleground site, Dyer prevents the cancellation of your Effect. In addition to posing a danger to characters, they should also cause your opponent to think twice about playing with too many vehicles, since Droidekas enjoy blowing them away too! Any target that is hit by these dangerous droids is also drilled with an additional 1 Force loss, which really adds insult to injury. Two of them can hold down a site, able to Force drain and draw battle destiny, and with an armor of 3 they will prove tough to eliminate in a fight. Combos: Playing with multiples of these droids makes that old Premiere Effect stronger than ever. When your opponent moves an EPP (or a powerful character armed with a lightsaber, like Jedi [[Luke Skywalker{{!}}Luke]] or Qui-Gon) to block your Force drain, they are vulnerable to losing their weapon on your next control phase! Pile up some Droidekas with her at the Droid Workshop, Droid Junkheap or the Incinerator and unleash big Force drains on your enemy. Don't forget that the retrieval part of this card targets any non-unique character, not just aliens! With his ambition agenda, he gets an extra bonus when drawn for destiny if you have flipped [[My Lord, Is That Legal? / I Will Make It Legal{{!}}My Lord, Is That Legal?]] Since he has a trade agenda, if he's on This is Outrageous!, you can use him to 'trade' unneeded cards in hand for a shot at a needed card from your Lost Pile. His blockade agenda is also useful, even if he's not at the Senate. When on Our Blockade is Perfectly Legal, he helps you 'blockade' your opponent by hindering your opponent's out of phase movement. But he also helps you when he's on the table, imagine that! With his blockade agenda, he lets you flip [[My Lord, Is That Legal? / I Will Make It Legal{{!}}My Lord, Is That Legal?]] with one less senator. But perhaps more importantly, if you have political control of the Galactic Senate, he gives you access to an incredibly powerful ability. Letting you look through your Force Pile allows you to take a key card into hand; it could be a critical character you need to battle, a matching weapon for your [[Darth Maul]], or any other card, it can all be yours, if you have a Senate majority. And in a pinch he helps his fellow Neimoidians out by adding to their forfeit Combos: Opponent who can't run away and who can't react! Chance to turn unneeded cards into crucial lost resources, only fate will decide. Loser (lowest total) is lost. |printings='''Decipher''' — '''this page''' (12_153) |sources=* [https://web.archive.org/web/20081225225012/http://www.decipher.com/starwars/cardlists/index.html Star Wars CCG cardlists index] at Decipher.com (archive, 25 December 2008) * [https://web.archive.org/web/20070928014432/http://www.decipher.com/starwars/cardlists/swallcards.pdf Complete Card List] (Decipher PDF, archive 28 September 2007) — Dark Interrupt: Maul Strikes, Coruscant, R |strategy=By [mailto:joea@decipher.com Joe Alread, Decipher Game Designer]https://web.archive.org/web/20040811123219/http://www.decipher.com/starwars/cardlists/coruscant/dark/small/maulstrikes.html The biggest complaint about [[Darth Maul]] from [[Tatooine (Dark) (Premiere){{!}}Tatooine]] was that his support cards were a bit weak when compared to [[Darth Vader]] or [[Ben Kenobi]]. Some things just take time, and [[Maul]] can happily take a big step up the main character chain with [[Maul Strikes]]. The three uses this card has are all extremely powerful. When you draw this card, one of its uses will almost certainly be needed immediately. Light Side players have been able to pull Lightsabers out of their decks for years with [[Gift Of The Mentor]], and now [[Maul Strikes]] allows the Dark Side to finally have their turn at this great ability. Another minor weakness of the [[Tatooine (Dark) (Premiere){{!}}Tatooine]] persona of [[Darth Maul]] was that his ability to duel was a bit restricted, since he had to essentially survive an entire turn before he had the chance to duel anybody. With [[Maul Strikes]], however, the Sith Lord can bypass that restriction, and duel at any time by simply playing this interrupt. And finally, if you're looking for just some good old beatdown, [[Maul]] can add battle destiny with this card too. Instead of just dueling Qui-Gon and making him lost, why not battle him, cut him, and draw three battle destiny as well?
